title: Kotlin
description: Expressive JVM & Android development with Kotlin idioms and coroutines.

chapters.title: Kotlin on the JVM
objectives: Explain the core ideas behind JVM and val/var.
Write and run working Kotlin code that uses JVM, val/var, REPL.
Recognise and avoid the common pitfalls associated with interop.
notes: Note — Kotlin on the JVM: JVM / val/var / REPL / interop are the heart of this chapter. Read the sample, then type it yourself.
Good practice: keep every example short and runnable; add a comment that records the expected output exactly.
International standard: every topic points to its section in the appendix and lists revisable key terms at the end.

exercises.question: What is the purpose of JVM in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: JVM lets you interop — see chapter section 1.2.

exercises.question: Modify the example to keep three decimal places instead of two.
exercises.answer: Format the printed value with the language's precision formatter (e.g. printf/round), then re-run and compare.

exercises.question: When would you avoid interop?
exercises.answer: Avoid it when the task is better served by a simpler, linear approach — momentum matters more than cleverness.

tests.instructions: One assessment per chapter grouping plus a final exam. Every question maps to the section shown in brackets so you can revise precisely.

questions.q: Which concept makes JVM behave that way? (Kotlin ch.1)
The worked sample prints "Hello from Kotlin". Which statement caused it? (ch.1)
Which concept makes ? behave that way? (Kotlin ch.2)
The worked sample prints "fallback". Which statement caused it? (ch.2)
Which concept makes fun behave that way? (Kotlin ch.3)
The worked sample prints "Hello Alio". Which statement caused it? (ch.3)
Which concept makes data class behave that way? (Kotlin ch.4)
The worked sample prints "Cart(items=2, total=45.0)". Which statement caused it? (ch.4)
Which concept makes suspend behave that way? (Kotlin ch.5)
The worked sample prints "Both loads run concurrently". Which statement caused it? (ch.5)
Which concept makes Activity behave that way? (Kotlin ch.6)
The worked sample prints "A composable renders Kotlin". Which statement caused it? (ch.6)

assessment.q: Write Kotlin code that reads a value, transforms it and prints the result. (final)
What does the score of 16.7 marks per chapter tell you about this exam's structure? (final)

glossary.meaning: A named container that stores a value in memory.
A reusable block of code that performs a task.
A construct that repeats a block of code while a condition holds.
The environment in which a program executes.
A special value representing the absence of data.
The set of rules that defines valid statements in a language.
